en.title: Weather and seasons
en.goal: Talk about the weather and the seasons of the year.

lessons.tempo-bonito-frio-quente: Describing the weather: nice, cold and hot

phrases.scenario: You're about to go out and want to know what the weather is like outside. What do you ask?
Someone asks what the weather is like, and today it's very hot. What do you answer?
Someone asks your favorite season, and it's winter. What do you say?
Someone asks what autumn is like in your city, with frequent rain. What do you say?

phrases.t: It snows a lot in winter.

il-fait-vs-jai.title: "Il fait chaud" or "j'ai chaud"?
il-fait-vs-jai.body: To talk about the weather, French uses the verb faire: il fait chaud (it's hot outside). To talk about a feeling of your own, it uses avoir: j'ai chaud (I'm hot, I feel hot). Watch out: "I am hot/cold" must not become je suis chaud/froid, which means something else; say j'ai chaud / j'ai froid. Impersonal "il" is for the weather, "je" for yourself.

trueFalse.claim: This sentence describes how a person is feeling.
trueFalse.whyNote: Wrong — il fait chaud describes the WEATHER (it's hot), not how someone feels. The "il" here is impersonal, as in "it's hot out."

review.why: 'il fait beau' = 'it's nice out'; chose full phrase.

review.pt: Eu prefiro o verão, está quente.
review.why: Informal 'tu' dialogue; reason clause rendered loosely.
